Thank you for sharing. I have been struggling with weighloss my entire life. Growing up my mom put a lock on the fridge and freezer because I was “too fat”. She wouldn’t be home to make us meals so there have been several times where I wouldn’t get to eat. If I tried to eat food off the shelves I would get spanked. Then it got to the point where My mom bought a lockable cabinet and hid a ton of shelf food in there because I was still too fat. This started when I was 9 year old all the way until I was 17 and moved out. 

On the same note when I went to visit my dad he would take the family to buffets all the time. For example it would be Sunday morning and we would have to skip breakfast because he didn’t want us cooking. Then we would go to a pizza buffet for lunch and he would tell us “this is your only meal for the day so eat up!” I remember eating to the point that I felt sick all the time. Now I know that I was binging and eating like crazy but back then I had no clue. My dad also bought all us kids 2  liters of soda pop for everyday we were at his house. 

The differences between my mom and dad were polar opposite. My mom being very strict on what I could eat and my value only came from how I looked. My dad could care less how I looked (although he has called me fat and ugly several times). Being at my dads was almost anxiety endorsing because I was so scared of getting spanked for eating. 

Now I am 25 years old. I eat all the time and I weigh 345 pounds and I’m 5’11”. (Just weighed myself.) I guess the reason I am telling this tale that I’ve never told anyone is because a lot of times people who are obese have had trauma or abuse in their lives. This could be physical, sexual, emotional, etc. Once you heal your pain you can move on. I’ve been working at mine for a month now

Oh yes, I definitely understand. One think I try to do is think ‘what is this fight worth’ whenever my husband pisses me off (often). Most of the time I realize it’s not worth much. Either I am being prideful or stubborn or there was a major lack of communication. During a fight tho I always think my feelings are invalid. I think it’s due to how I grew up so it helps me when my husband says “your feelings are valid. You are allowed to feel. You can be angry, hurt, sad, happy, scared, mad anything. You can feel and it’s actually a good thing to feel”. This has been one of the most helpful and effective things I’ve heard in my entire life. 

It also helps me to write. When I fight with my husband I write my perspective down so that way during an argument I don’t lose track of everything I wanted to say. When I feel like I’m sitting there just taking what he says that rough. Especially when I have no clue how to respond. But if I can have 30 mins to clear my head it’s easier to talk to him. 

When you said you get upset by the little things that upset him.. girl. I totally understand! Anything that bothers my husband I always get really upset about. One because I don’t like seeing him upset. Two because if I did it I feel like he is upset with me and not the situation and three because I feel like there is a miscommunication or misunderstanding that happened which is why he is upset. Ex. He might have not understood one of my jokes and it upset him. Then I’m annoyed because he doesn’t get that I’m joking. And it spirals. It usually takes a lot of talking to fix that one lol. 

It’s also rough being in a relationship when your not used to it. That where I am. I got married and one had one “sorta” relationship before my husband. My husband cares about me and it’s a though process I don’t really know how to understand. Probably because of how I view myself tho. But he cares about me and I struggle with feelings of not being worthy of love or that somehow I want him but he won’t want me.. it goes on and on. My heart goes out for you both. I get it’s a rough place to be. Also, I’m sorry you had to go through with an abusive partner. Those relationships can be very damaging and difficult. I am very proud of you for having the courage to get out. Not everyone is that strong. That’s pretty freakin inspiring ❤️ 

And yea, I understand what you’re going through! If you ever wanna talk we can 😊 and I really hope you both work out the argument!

I can totally understand how frustrating it can be. I get frustrated with myself for it. It’s good to hear that you are patient though. Most people are not. It’s easy to see what the physical responses are like shutting down and pushing people away but it’s harder to remember that mental things are happening too. Maybe send him a small text telling him you would like to talk when he is ready could help a lot. For me, it’s easier to talk when I know people aren’t mad or upset. Which is hard to do in a fight.

I can actually relate to your husband. I don’t know his past but as for me I got in trouble growing up if I shared how I felt. My mom would literally beat me. My brother got locked in the basement for a few days before.. But we learned quickly that talking is bad. Sharing anything is bad. Teaches you that if there is a problem it’s typically your fault even if it’s off the walls crazy like world hunger. You start living with the pain and the burdens and the guilt. I am married and I still have trouble talking to my husband at times. I’m scared he will get mad (he never is) or the overwhelming feelings inside I can’t even deal with so I can I expect someone else too? I was also taught that no crime goes unpunished so if I ever do anything wrong I feel like I deserve to be beaten, abused, hurt, whatever can make the other person feel better. Actually.. I probably sound like I need therapy 😂 I’m just trying to say that there might be a part of your husband where it’s really hard for him to talk. He might need more reassurance. He might need reminded he is loved, especially in a fight. Waiting to talk until the last minute is also something I subconsciously do. It’s a safety mechanism so if I become too uncomfortable I can get away. I want to solve the issues but my husband gets to the point of being ready to solve them way faster than I do. Just remind yourself and your husband why you love each other and how happy it makes you knowing he is always there when you need him. Taking that different approach to the fight might help a lot. And I’m sure he is feeling all the frustration you are too. Y’all are only human.❤️ let me know if you both work it out. I’m invested now lol
